priceSnapshot.note: The line held. That is the entire report. Overnight, in the 6h26m since the endday snapshot at 64,341.3, price traded down into the exact level this desk has been publishing for four sessions and bounced off it: the session low printed 64,159.6 at 05:11Z, which is NINE POINT SIX POINTS above the 64,150 reduce line and 29.6 points above the 64,130 resting stop the endday session recommended. Neither fired. The reduce trigger was a 1H CLOSE below 64,150 and the lowest completed hourly close of the night was 64,257.2, a full 107 points clear. What happened at that low was not a drift, it was a flush: OKX filled $125,745 of LONG liquidations against $3,607 of shorts in the 12.6-hour window, a 34.9-to-1 ratio, and the heaviest single burst - eleven fills inside 20 seconds at 05:32Z - landed at 64,134.4 to 64,162.7. Leveraged longs were carried out at the bottom and the level absorbed it. Price is now 64,316.4, back above the 4H EMA20 at 64,262.04 and 195 points above the daily EMA20 at 64,121.67, which will make a NINTH consecutive daily close above that line if it holds. Session range since the endday mark: low 64,159.6, high 64,549.9, a 390.3-point band worth 0.29 of a daily ATR. Short-term momentum has turned: the 15m MACD histogram is POSITIVE at +9.39 after printing -1.60 at the endday read, and the 1H histogram has repaired from -46.17 to -17.12. The 4H is the holdout - its histogram deepened from -17.38 to -33.48 - so this is a level that held with the medium-term still rolling over, not a completed turn.

reduceIf.confirmation: A 1H CLOSE below $64,150 - unchanged for a fifth consecutive session and now the most thoroughly tested line on the board. Overnight it was probed to 64,159.6 and rejected, which is the second distinct defence of the 64,150-64,175 shelf in 24 hours after the 64,172.6 low on 06 Aug. Price sits 166.4 points above it and the 1H ATR(14) is 200.14, so one average hour still spans the distance; the difference from last night is that the leveraged longs sitting above it have already been liquidated, which removes the fuel that makes a break self-reinforcing. A close below 64,150 now clears a level the market has twice paid to defend, and what is underneath is thin - only $4,278 of realized liquidations in the whole 64,050-64,149 band - down to the daily EMA20 at 64,121.67, which has held on closes for eight days. The warnings between spot and the line, in order: the 4H EMA20 at 64,262.04, the $26,842 pocket at 64,200 and the 64,159.6 session low.

addIf.confirmation: A 4H CLOSE above $64,650. This is a DELIBERATE CHANGE from the 65,030 level that has stood for four sessions, and the reason is that 65,030 has become a target rather than a trigger - it is 714 points away, it has rejected six times in 102 hours, and waiting for it has meant the desk sat out every repair. 64,650 is the honest intermediate: it reclaims the daily EMA50 at 64,627.43 and clears last night's 64,652.1 high and this session's 64,549.9 high in one move, which would end the lower-highs sequence that started at 17:00Z on 06 Aug. Above it, the next real obstacle is the CoinGlass forward magnet at 65,250 with almost nothing in between. 65,030 remains the level that restores a FULL bullish stance; 64,650 is the level that confirms the bounce is a turn.

decisionBox.changed: Position moves from HOLD to ADD, the tilt flips from BEARISH back to BULLISH, confidence rises from 5.1 to 5.4, the add trigger comes down from 65,030 to 64,650, and the resting stop stays at 64,130. Five things changed and four of them improved. FIRST and most important, the endday session's single named binary RESOLVED BULLISH. It flagged that the 06 Aug Farside row was incomplete at +9.3M with IBIT unreported and said tomorrow's midnight session should read it before anything else. It is now complete: IBIT printed +128.3M and the day totals +137.6M, not +9.3M. The ETF bid did not break; the streak is four straight positive days at 170.1, 211.5, 244.4 and 137.6. SECOND, the level held under a real test, and the way it held matters - a 34.9-to-1 long-liquidation flush into 64,134-64,163 and an immediate 157-point recovery is the signature of forced sellers being absorbed, not of distribution. THIRD, short-term momentum turned: the 15m MACD histogram crossed POSITIVE at +9.39 from -1.60 and the 1H histogram repaired from -46.17 to -17.12, while the daily histogram improved from -4.19 to -0.72 and is now within a rounding error of crossing back up. FOURTH, price reclaimed the 4H EMA20 at 64,262.04 which it was below at the endday mark. Set against that, ONE thing got worse and one is simply unknowable. The 4H MACD histogram deepened from -17.38 to -33.48, so the timeframe that flipped negative last night has kept falling, which is why this is a range call with a tilt and not a bullish call. And the US July jobs report lands at 07:30 COT today, into a market pricing a 25bp Fed HIKE in September, with Brent up 0.87% to 83.21 on renewed Strait of Hormuz tension. That is a genuine two-sided binary sitting between the morning and midday sessions, and it is the reason confidence is 5.4 and not higher.

calibration.note: The endday call was range with a bearish tilt, position HOLD, a reduce level of 64,150, an add level of 65,030 and a RECOMMENDED resting stop at 64,130. Neither level fired and the stop was not hit - but this was by far the narrowest margin of the week and it is the most instructive row in the log. The session low of 64,159.6 came within 9.6 points of the reduce line and within 29.6 points of the stop. Acting HELPED, and specifically two decisions helped. First, refusing to trim mid-box: the endday rationale argued that selling before the published level had fired would mean realising a loss in the middle of the range at exactly the prices that cost this desk money twice this week, and price is now 64,316.4 against the 64,341.3 mark, essentially flat, so a mid-box trim would have been a pure loss. Second, and more precisely, the choice to put the stop at 64,130 rather than at the reduce line or under the 64,172.6 low. A stop at 64,150 would have been filled. A stop at 64,172 would have been filled. 64,130 was placed below the twice-tested shelf and above the daily EMA20 on the explicit reasoning that it should exit on a structural break and not on a wick into the 64,200 pocket, and that is exactly what happened - the wick came, the pocket was consumed, and the stop survived by 29.6 points. The rolling record moves to 29 of 38. The lesson to carry forward is that stop PLACEMENT, not stop presence, was the whole edge here, and the placement rule that worked was: below the tested low, above the structural EMA, outside the nearest liquidation pocket.
